title: Health Care And A Blast From The Past
gist: Teaser only: Gavekal revisits the 'platform company' framework from its 2005 book Our Brave New World, in which Western firms keep design, R&D and marketing in-house and outsource capital-intensive, volatile manufacturing ('produce nowhere, sell everywhere'). The health-care application promised by the title is behind the paywall and not present in the visible text.

insights.claim: Gavekal's 2005 'platform company' framework holds that the vertical design/produce/sell business model (e.g. Ford designing, building in Detroit and selling an Expedition SUV via US dealers) gave way to a model of producing nowhere but selling everywhere.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: A lens for valuing firms by how much low-return production they have outsourced versus retained high-margin design and distribution.
insights.quote: The new business model is to produce nowhere, but sell everywhere.
insights.locator: Back in 2005, we published a book

insights.claim: Platform companies keep the high value-added functions of research, development, treasury and marketing in-house and farm out manufacturing to external producers, acting as organizers between client orders and producer delivery.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Margin and capital efficiency accrue to whoever controls the customer and the IP, not the factory.
insights.quote: Platform companies keep the high added-value parts of research, development, treasury and marketing in-house, and farm out all the rest to external producers
insights.locator: Platform companies know where the clients are

insights.claim: In Gavekal's framework, Western companies shun production because it ties up capital, is labor-intensive, requires expensive inventories, is highly volatile, and is not rewarded by equity markets.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Explains the market premium on asset-light, non-cyclical business models and the discount on capital-heavy producers.
insights.quote: out of the three things I do—designing, producing and selling—producing is a mug’s game.
insights.locator: An increasing number of Western companies

insights.claim: Gavekal's Louis-Vincent Gave-bylined note revives the 2005 platform-company thesis in the context of health care, implying the outsourcing/asset-light framework is relevant to the sector, though the actual argument is not visible in the teaser.
insights.speaker: Gavekal Research
insights.so_what: Flag for follow-up: the full piece may argue health-care firms are adopting or should adopt a platform model; unverifiable from this text.
insights.locator: Health Care And A Blast From The Past
